decision: Replace the Google Maps native point with the application-site centroid that the Greater London Authority's Planning London Datahub publishes for Islington planning application P102023 (extension of the five existing flues serving five diesel generators at 260-270 Goswell Road, approved 29 September 2011).
geometry_note: The WGS84 centroid is copied as published. As a check, pyproj 3.7.1 (EPSG:27700 to EPSG:4326, always_xy) turns the published British National Grid centroid 531829 E, 182810 N into -0.1009672, 51.5288196, within 0.1 m of the published WGS84 value.

site_polygon_check.polygon: The record's British National Grid site polygon has 14 vertices and 461.3 m2 (bounds 531817.8-531841.1 E, 182789.2-182831.0 N; about 23 m by 42 m along the Goswell Road frontage), matching the recorded site area of 0.046 ha.

same_premises_records: The same UPRN 5300036858, polygon and centroid carry Islington's 1999 'Proposed use as an IP Gateway (Telecommunications)' decision (991151, which notes the premises' lawful use as a distillery and bottling plant) and the 2018 S73 variation of the generator air-quality and emergency-generator management conditions (P2017/2113/S73).
newer_records: Islington's 2026 records for '260 - 266 Goswell Road' (P2026/0587/FUL, replacement of plant and associated works to roof, approved 28 April 2026; P2026/2242/MIN, pre-application advice on two additional generators and three additional chillers, 14 October 2026) use a newer UPRN 10094612777 whose published centroid (51.529057, -0.100107; 531888 E, 182838 N) lies 65 m north-east of the new point and 57 m outside the 2011 polygon, and declare a site area of 0.632 ha. The full premises therefore extend beyond the 461 m2 frontage polygon; its outline is not published in the datahub.
transform: pyproj 3.7.1, shapely 2.1.1 (check only; the locator is the published WGS84 centroid)
identity_bridge: Stellanor's London North page gives 260-266 Goswell Road, Angel, London EC1V 7EB, describes the building as the former Gordon's Gin Distillery and says the data centre opened in 2000; Islington's records at the same postcode and street numbers cover the 1999 change of use of the former distillery and bottling plant to an IP gateway, the data centre's diesel-generator flues (2011), and 2026 roof-plant replacement and generator and chiller additions.
nearby_records_within_2km: Only this site (curated:stellanor-london-north-goswell, 11 m from the new point) in verified_construction_core/2026-11-07-research-hundredtwentieth; no pending queue addition or locator correction within 2 km.
